Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) is a greedy algorithm used in sparse coding to find an approximate sparse solution $\mathbf{x}$ for the problem $\min \|\mathbf{x}\|_0$ subject to $\|\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{D}\mathbf{x}\|_2 \leq \epsilon$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) is a greedy algorithm used to find an approximate solution for the sparse coding problem. Specifically, Source [S1] notes define OMP as selecting dictionary atoms sequentially to find an approximate sparse solution x for the problem min ||x||_0 subject to ||y - Dx||_2 <= epsilon. The passages further confirm that OMP is a greedy algorithm similar to MP, used to find approximate solutions because exact sparsest representation is NP-hard. The claim accurately reflects the definition and purpose of OMP as described in the provided text.
supported

Therefore, the evidence confirms that L is the upper bound (maximum) on the number of nonzero entries in the coefficient vector.
